 Some Social Security recipients will get their November payments this week
 Bailey Allen, USA TODAY NETWORK - New England 2026년 10월 27일 화 오후 4:59 UTC 0 Some Social Security recipients will receive their benefit checks earlier than usual this November.
 The Social Security Administration  will send its first round of regular November 2026 benefits on Tuesday, Nov. 10, a day earlier, because Veterans Day falls on that Wednesday, according to the  SSA's calendar . All Social Security offices will be closed for the federal holiday on Nov. 11.
 Supplemental Security Income (SSI)  recipients will also receive their November payments early – on Friday, Oct. 30, because Nov. 1 is on a Sunday this year.
 Recipients should also be aware of changes to the way the Social Security Administration delivers payments. The SSA plans to fully transition to electronic payments by the end of the year. In addition, Fifth Third Bank is replacing Comerica Bank as the financial agent for the Direct Express debit card program, the SSA said in a May 18 notice .
 Looking ahead to next year, the SSA just announced a 3.6% cost-of-living adjustment for 2027, which is expected to increase monthly checks by about $56 starting in January.
 In Rhode Island, more than  241,000 people rely on Social Security payments  every month, according to Congressional Statistics from December 2024. Nearly  71 million Americans  get Social Security, and 7.4 million get SSI, according to January 2026 numbers from the SSA.
 Here's what to know about November Social Security payments.
 Social Security payment schedule for November 2026
 The Social Security Administration's yearly distribution schedules for  2026  and 2027 are available online for recipients to use for budgeting purposes. Regular Social Security retirement benefits are slated to be distributed on the SSA's usual schedule based on birth date:
 Tuesday, Nov. 10:  Birth dates between the 1st and 10th of the month.
 Wednesday, Nov. 18:  Birth dates between the 11th and 20th of the month.
 Wednesday, Nov. 25:  Birth dates between the 21st and 31st of the month.
 Those who began getting benefits before May 1997 will be paid on Tuesday, Nov. 3.
 Recipients of Supplemental Security Income checks will be issued their November payments on Friday, Oct. 30.
 What is SSI?
 Supplemental Security Income (SSI) provides monthly benefits to those with limited income or resources who are 65 or older, blind, or have a qualifying disability. Children with a qualifying disability can also get SSI,  according to the SSA's website .
 Advertisement
 Adults who qualify for SSI generally do not have  monthly wages above $2,073 .
 Those eligible for SSI can begin the application process  online , in person at your local  Social Security office or by calling 1-800-772-1213 (TTY 1-800-325-0778) from 8 a.m. to 7 p.m. local time during the work week.
 SSI payment schedule for 2026 and early 2027
 SSI checks will be sent out on the following dates in 2026 and early 2027,  according to the SSA calendar :
 Friday, Oct. 30, 2026: November 2026 payment
 Tuesday, Dec. 1, 2026: December 2026 payment
 Thursday, Dec. 31, 2026: January 2027 payment
 Monday, Feb. 1, 2027: February 2027 payment
 Monday, March 1, 2027: March 2027 payment
 Thursday, April 1, 2027: April 2027 payment
 Friday, April 30, 2027: May 2027 payment
 Tuesday, June 1, 2027: June 2027 payment
 What do I do if my scheduled payment date passes without payment?
 The Social Security Administration suggests that if you don’t receive your payment on the expected date, allow three additional mailing days before contacting the agency. Most will arrive on time because 99% of beneficiaries are paid electronically.
 Where is a Social Security office in Rhode Island?
 In Rhode Island, there are five Social Security offices . Here's where:
 380 Westminster St., Providence, RI 02903
 4 Pleasant St., Pawtucket, RI 02860
 30 Quaker Ln., Warwick, RI 02886
 130 Bellevue Ave., Newport, RI 02840
 2168 Diamond Hill Rd, Woonsocket, RI 02895
 There's also one Disability Determination Service office and one Remote Hearing Site in Rhode Island. To find the one closest to you, use the  Social Security Office Locator .
 When can you start collecting Social Security?
 Everyone can start receiving reduced Social Security benefits as early as age 62. However, waiting until full retirement age results in a larger monthly payment. That age has  gradually increased in recent years , rising by two months for each successive birth year.
 For example , if you were born in 1958, your full retirement age is 66 years and 8 months, while those born in 1959 reach it at 66 years and 10 months. For anyone born in 1960 or later, the full retirement age is 67.
 You can calculate your full retirement age on the SSA website.
 Mike Snider and Medora Lee of USA TODAY contributed to this report.
